title: Export PIM Manager settings to a settings document (settings as code)
purpose: Exports PIM Manager settings (for example the naming conventions) from one environment's store to a settings document (a JSON file) that Import-PimSettings.ps1 applies to another environment: settings as code, never secrets, never identity or access settings.
whenToRun: When an environment's settings should be kept as code (in source control, reviewed) or used as the baseline for a new environment. Settings that are secrets or that name the environment itself (who may use it, approvers, break-glass accounts, demo mode, environment name, licence and install keys, rings, the scenario, runtime state) are never exported: a -Name that asks for one is refused, -All leaves them out and lists them.

runAs.name: Store reader (application with a certificate, member of the environment's SQL admin group)
runAs.why: Reads the settings to export. The identity is given with -ClientId / -CertThumbprint and its certificate must be in the local machine certificate store.

changes.object: the settings document at -Path (one JSON file)
changes.why: The point of the script: the exported settings, ready for Import-PimSettings.ps1. An existing file is replaced only with -Force.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.help: The setting(s) to export, e.g. NamingConventions. Give -Name or -All.

parameters.name: All
parameters.help: Export every setting that may be exported; the others are listed as skipped.

parameters.name: ClientId
parameters.help: Application (client) id of the identity that reads the store.

parameters.name: CertThumbprint
parameters.help: Thumbprint of that identity's certificate in the local machine store.

readsOnly: pim.Settings in the store (the named settings, or every name with -All, and the environment name)
network: login.microsoftonline.com (tokens for Azure SQL, certificate sign-in)
whatIf: Reads the store, lists each setting it would export (and each one it skips, with the reason) and prints 'What if: Performing the operation "write the settings document (<n> setting(s))" on target "<Path>"'. Nothing is written.
undo: The script changes nothing in any environment. Delete the settings document it wrote.
